newsitem.title: USA: Cox not seeking computer co investment.
newsitem.headline: Cox not seeking computer co investment.

text.p: Cable operator Cox Communications Inc is not interested in an equity investment by a computer company, like Microsoft Corp's $1 billion stake in cable rival Comcast Corp, James Robbins, Cox president and chief executive, said Tuesday.
"I'd never say never on any item like that, but we're not looking for any extra equity in the company at this point," Robbins said in an interview.
Saying that Cox already has "benefited from their investment in Comcast, without having to sell shares," Robbins cited the rise in Cox's stock price.
On June 6, the Friday before the June 9 announcement by Microsoft, shares closed at 18-1/4. At midday Tuesday, shares traded at 27-15/16.
Microsoft in June invested $1 billion to buy 24.6 million shares of Class A special Comcast common.
Robbins said he talked with Larry Ellison, chairman of Oracle Corp, in recent weeks, but characterized those as general industry discussions.
Ellison has reportedly been seeking to make an investment similar to the one by Microsoft. Oracle officials were not immediately available for comment.

Robbins said Cox plans to unload several non-cable investments totaling $4-$5 billion. "We have a number of off-balance sheets we're figuring out ways to liquidate," he said. "If we found a way to liquidate, I would."
Robbins said Cox was "working on a number of them simultaneously," but declined to provide details.

Such investments include a 14.65 percent stake in the U.K. cable company Telewest Communications Plc ; a position in Teleport Communications Group Inc, which provides local telecommunications services, valued at about $1.5 billion; as well as stakes in the Sprint PCS partnership, and the PrimeStar satellite TV partnership.
"We believe that, at our size, we can't do everything. We need to focus on our core businesses," Robbins said.
"The strategy play here is to demonstrate to the Street that we will continue to make investments in (our) core businesses," he said.

Cox currently has about 3.2 million basic cable subscribers in the United States, making it the fifth largest operator in the country. Robbins said he expects subscriber growth at about two percent this year.
"(Subscriber) growth will be harder," he said, adding that, instead, growth will come from selling other services, such as local telephone.

Cox will make a "fullblown launch" of phone service to subscribers in Orange County, Calif., during the third quarter. He declined to say what expectations were for the number of customers or revenues.
Robbins said he did not expect privately held Cox Enterprises to unload more of its holdings in the company to the public. Cox Enterprises currently holds a 75.2 percent stake in the cable company.

Dallas Clement, Cox Communication's treasurer, said in the interview, that the company expects cash flow to increase in the high single digits to low double digits this year from $556.9 million in 1996.
